definitions.gloss: a yakitori skewer of chicken alternating with pieces of leek
definitions.explanation: The standard yakitori skewer on which chunks of chicken thigh alternate with sections of {長|なが}ねぎ. Usually the first thing ordered at a yakitori shop and the benchmark by which the shop is judged.

examples.japanese: ねぎまをタレでお{願|ねが}いします。
この{店|みせ}のねぎまは{肉|にく}が{厚|あつ}くておいしい。
examples.english: The negima at this place has thick pieces of meat and tastes great.

examples.japanese: とりあえずねぎまと{砂肝|すなぎも}を{頼|たの}んで、{飲|の}み{物|もの}はあとで{決|き}めよう。
examples.english: Let's order negima and gizzard for now and decide on drinks later.

notes:
Written in kana on almost every menu. The name comes from ねぎ (leek) plus ま, and originally referred to an Edo-period dish of leek and tuna ({鮪|まぐろ}); the chicken skewer took over the name later.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ねぎまをタレで: negima with the sweet soy sauce
- ねぎまを{塩|しお}で: negima with salt
- ねぎま{二本|にほん}: two negima skewers

USAGE:
Ordering yakitori means choosing タレ (sauce) or {塩|しお} (salt) for each item, so ねぎまを{塩|しお}で is a complete order on its own.
